items.title: Jack Teagarden Interview, 1959-10-29
items.q: And, uh, of course, uh, Debussy and, uh, and Ravel. And he made, uh, put all this with his ideas.

ctx.x: You know, he seems to me to have been so wonderful and to develop a lot of things that, you know, from what I've heard from Len Harrell and guys who listen to him. Yeah. Yeah. Like the guy who worked with Jimmy Joy, Len Harrell, I'm talking about. Yeah. He must have heard a lot of classical music too, huh?

Yeah. He went, he made a, he made a real study of piano. He used to practice about eight hours a day. And, uh, he taught himself to read and then he, uh, went for Chopin mostly. And, uh, of course, uh, Debussy and, uh, and Ravel. And he made, uh, put all this with his ideas. And, uh, of course he knows Boogie Woogie and, uh, and the Earl Hines style of piano. He was playing long before, way before Earl Hines. And I guess it, uh, never been heard by anybody. He was sort of, uh, Art Tatum maybe. Uh, Art Tatum and…

Well, to me, and when I listen to your style, I see that you have developed such a clean technique and developed the trombone so much further than the people that were before you. I believe myself. Yeah.
